name: adidnsdump - Dump All AD DNS Records
description: Dumps all DNS records from Active Directory Integrated DNS via LDAP. By default, any authenticated user can query all DNS records in the domain — including internal hosts, servers, and infrastructure that doesn't appear in normal DNS lookups (hidden records). Reveals the full internal network map.
source: CPTS Module 13: Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks
notes:
=== WHY AD DNS ENUMERATION MATTERS ===
AD Integrated DNS stores all domain DNS records in AD itself (not just on the DNS
server). Any authenticated domain user can read these records via LDAP — including
records that would normally be hidden from external DNS queries.

This reveals:
  - Internal server names and IPs (web servers, file servers, databases, etc.)
  - Infrastructure you didn't know existed (backup servers, monitoring, etc.)
  - Naming conventions that reveal purpose (SQL01, BACKUP01, MGMT, etc.)
  - Cross-forest DNS delegations and trust infrastructure

=== THE -r FLAG ===
  Without -r: only queries the domain zone (e.g., INLANEFREIGHT.LOCAL)
  With -r:    tries to resolve additional records that may not appear directly
              (forest DNS, _msdcs zone, etc.)

=== OUTPUT ===
adidnsdump saves to records.csv with columns:
  name, type, value (IP), TTL
Good sources: filter for A records (IPs) and identify unknown hosts to target next.

=== USING THE OUTPUT ===
1. Build a full internal network map
2. Find hosts you haven't scanned yet
3. Discover naming patterns → guess other hosts
4. Find management infrastructure (out-of-band mgmt, backup, monitoring)
5. Identify web servers and APIs → check for web vulns

=== EXAMPLE PIVOT ===
Find SQL01.INLANEFREIGHT.LOCAL → 172.16.5.150 → nmap → MSSQL open →
PowerUpSQL → sysadmin access → xp_cmdshell → SYSTEM on DB server

references.title: HTB Academy - Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks

defense.why_it_works: adidnsdump enumerates records from AD-Integrated DNS (readable by authenticated users), revealing internal hostnames/IPs including hidden ones.
defense.prerequisites: Valid domain credentials and LDAP access to the DC.
defense.impact: An internal DNS map (hostnames/IPs) that broadens the target list.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1018] LDAP queries against the DNS partition (4662); one host reading the DNS zone.
defense.artifacts: LDAP queries to the AD DNS partition; the dumped records.
defense.prevention: Monitor LDAP reads of the DNS partition; least privilege; the data is readable by design so detection is primary.
defense.evasion: A single scoped query blends with normal LDAP; the read is legitimate for any domain user.
defense.misconfiguration: Active-Directory-Integrated DNS stores every DNS record as an object in AD. The default ACL lets any authenticated domain user read the whole zone over LDAP (adidnsdump), exposing all internal hostnames, IPs, and naming conventions - including records hidden from normal DNS queries. The exposure is the default read access on the DNS partition, not a zone-transfer (AXFR) misconfiguration; adidnsdump never issues AXFR.
